title: When anything can be an arrow
question: What does a collection of things need before it counts as a vector space?
hook: Arrows, polynomials and functions can all play by the same rules.
idea: A vector space is anything you can add and scale by the rules, and its dimension counts the vectors in any basis.

beats.prompt: A guide says: go 3 miles north. Then: go 4 miles east. Then adds: take one move of 3 miles north plus 4 miles east together. On a flat map, what does the third instruction do?

choices.label: It gives new information the first two lack
choices.feedback: It sounds like extra detail, but the first two already fix the spot.

choices.label: It adds nothing new, being a combination of the first two
It contradicts the first two
choices.feedback: It is true; it is simply not necessary to find the location.

beats.explain: The third move is a linear combination of the other two, so no element is needed beyond them: the set is not linearly independent.

beats.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.
pairs: A vector built by scaling and adding chosen vectors
The smallest subspace containing a group of vectors
Independent vectors that span the whole space
The number of vectors in any basis
beats.explain: Each idea builds on the last: combinations make spans, spans plus independence make bases, and bases give dimension.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: A basis is a group of independent vectors that spans the space.
Anna finds a basis for a space, and it has 3 vectors.
Ben picks a different basis for the same space.
So Ben's basis can have a different number of vectors than Anna's.
beats.explain: All bases of a vector space have the same number of vectors, and that number is the dimension.

beats.prompt: Two vector spaces over the same field have the same dimension. What do they share?

choices.label: Every property that depends only on the vector-space structure
Exactly the same set of elements
choices.feedback: Their elements can be entirely different kinds of objects.

choices.label: Nothing, since dimension is only a count
choices.feedback: The count turns out to settle all structural properties.

beats.explain: Same field and same dimension means the spaces are isomorphic, so structural properties match.
